title: AI is Automated Inference
content: “AI is not artificial, nor is it intelligent; it is simply Automated Inference.” AI models infer from learned patterns and the context supplied. The slide states that more accurate source data reduces hallucination and energy use at data centers.

title: AI Models are Trained; Teach yours well
content: Training shapes a model’s learned patterns. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) supplies source evidence when a user enters a prompt and triggers a RAG tool. A person's contribution to the AI ecosystem starts with a precise identity record that makes permissioned information about that person accessible to AI models.

title: Create Your Own "Verified and Validated" Introduction: A Soulbound Token (SBT)
content: An SBT is an identity record bound to its subject, with structured claims, evidence and permissions. A “Verified” source authenticates who created or issued the record. A “Validated” claim is checked by an identified third party against evidence and recorded as validated or not validated.

title: Same prompt, two sources
content: Prompt: “Who has experience with winter road safety modeling?” The slide contrasts an ambiguous PDF résumé entry with an SBT structured record. The SBT explicitly identifies the claim, topic, evidence, dates, and validator, making the topic explicit, evidence linked, and reviewer identified.

title: A cookie package label makes the object’s content identifiable
content: A cookie package label makes an object's content identifiable through descriptors such as product, ingredients, allergen notices, manufacturer, and lot/best-by information. Each descriptor tells a buyer what the object is.

title: A machine-readable label travels with the object
content: Illustrative JSON label fields include product, flavor, manufacturer, lot_id, and evidence. Named fields describe the object; semantic embeddings help find it; evidence supports checking it. Supply-chain receipts can reference the label and lot across different buyers and intermediaries.

title: One identity, two readable formats
content: The same identity can have a machine-readable JSON record and a human-readable SBT. The machine-readable form supports reviewing claims and evidence links, inspecting validation status and permissions, and checking pending approval and signature. The human-readable form supports reviewing identity and credentials and comparing them with the machine-readable record.

title: One AI agent answers the user’s prompt
content: Prompt: “Which registered member has experience with transportation planning?” Proposed workflow: User prompt → AI agent plans the query → RAG target authorizes and retrieves → AI agent reasons from evidence → user receives answer plus sources. Demo result: Priya Shah, Transportation Planner, Demo Mobility Lab; the demo labels the returned expertise as transportation planning.

title: Your identity needs governance
content: For the record: define claims and approve the canonical source, then correct and version it when experience changes. For permissions: set access and attribution terms for original content and specify licensing or compensation where applicable. Proposal: an Engineering School-controlled repository could let students opt in, create their own SBTs, validate claims, and test retrievals.

title: Remember
content: Three closing points: the presentation frames AI as neither “Artificial” nor “Intelligent”; individuals should define who they are and set rules and permissions for AI tools to access personal and professional identifiers; understanding how to define oneself to the agentic AI ecosystem can help tame broader AI tools for use as a trusted assistant.
